posts.title: Weight-loss drugs show signs of slowing biological aging, say drugmakers
posts.summary: Popular weight-loss drugs may do more than help people shed pounds. They might also melt away the years. Drug giants Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk say patients taking their drugs age less quickly, according to readouts from molecular “aging clocks.” Such clocks assess a person’s biological age by looking at changes to DNA that accumulate…
bullets: Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk report that GLP-1 receptor agonists demonstrate the potential to reduce biological age by two to three years, as measured by molecular aging clocks.
These aging clocks track DNA changes and protein levels to assess biological decline, with researchers suggesting GLP-1 drugs may function as 'geroprotectors' that slow or reverse aging processes.
While the drugs are currently indicated for weight loss and diabetes, their observed benefits in improving kidney function and reducing mortality suggest a broader impact on systemic health span.

Experts caution that while the anti-aging effects appear significant in unhealthy populations, the efficacy and safety of these drugs for healthy individuals remain unproven and require further study.

posts.title: Thermal Complexity Grows With AI Chips And Photonics
posts.summary:
Increasing power density makes heat, stress, and aging harder to predict, and more critical to address earlier in the design flow.
The post Thermal Complexity Grows With AI Chips And Photonics appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Increasing power density in AI chips is making heat, stress, and aging effects significantly harder to predict, necessitating thermal management strategies earlier in the design cycle.
While photonics offers a path to reduce data center bottlenecks, the technology faces scalability hurdles due to high component losses and the need for complex, heat-sensitive control structures.
Large-scale photonic mesh switches require thousands of integrated heaters for calibration, creating a new layer of thermal management complexity that must be solved to achieve performance stability.

Industry experts suggest that moving toward modular, scalable architectures and co-packaged optics is essential to manage the disparate heat profiles generated by heterogeneous processing elements like GPUs and CPUs.

posts.title: Memory At The Edge: Non-Volatile Memory Challenges And Requirements For Humanoid Robots
posts.summary:
Distributed NVM supports high-endurance telemetry logging, functional safety, and time-sensitive networking where resilience is critical.
The post Memory At The Edge: Non-Volatile Memory Challenges And Requirements For Humanoid Robots appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Humanoid robot shipments are projected to scale from 15,000 units in 2025 to over 6 million annually by 2035, driving demand for specialized memory architectures.
Robotic systems require a multi-tier memory strategy, balancing high-bandwidth storage for AI inference with latency-optimized memory for deterministic motor control.
High-frequency telemetry logging for safety and regulatory compliance is pushing the endurance limits of conventional non-volatile memory, necessitating more robust storage solutions.

posts.title: Programmable Memory Controller Eases Adoption of New DRAM Techniques (ETH Zürich, CISPA, NYU)
posts.summary:
Researchers at ETH Zürich, CISPA, and New York University published a technical paper titled “Terracotta: Enabling the Adoption of New DRAM Techniques via a Flexible DRAM Interface and Memory Controller.” Abstract Excerpt: “DRAM continues to limit the performance, energy efficiency, and robustness of modern systems. Many prior works propose DRAM techniques that support in-DRAM computation,... » read more
The post Programmable Memory Controller Eases Adoption of New DRAM Techniques (ETH Zürich, CISPA, NYU) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Researchers from ETH Zürich, CISPA, and NYU have introduced 'Terracotta,' a framework designed to overcome the rigid limitations of current DRAM interfaces and memory controllers.
The framework utilizes custom command extensions and a programmable memory controller to allow system designers to implement new DRAM techniques post-silicon without requiring hardware redesigns.
By standardizing a set of primitives for diverse DRAM operations, Terracotta aims to accelerate the adoption of in-DRAM computation, improved latency, and enhanced reliability features.
This approach addresses the industry bottleneck where adopting new memory innovations typically requires repeated, costly modifications to standardized memory controller structures.
